items.headline: Kandinsky sets an $85.8m auction record
items.summary: His Bauhaus-era painting Betonte Ecken sold at Christie's New York on 17 November, nearly doubling his previous record.
items.question: Whose painting Betonte Ecken set an $85.8m auction record?
items.explain: Kandinsky painted it in Weimar in 1922 to 1923 while teaching at the Bauhaus; his previous record was $44.8m, set at Sotheby's London in 2023.

notes.Paul Klee: Klee taught at the Bauhaus alongside Kandinsky, but this record painting is not his.

items.headline: Van Gogh sets a $190m auction record
items.summary: Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold for $190.4m with fees at Sotheby's New York on 18 November, far above his previous record of $117.2m.
items.question: Which Van Gogh sold for a record $190m in New York on 18 November?
items.explain: He painted it at Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890, in the last weeks of his life; it beat the $117.2m paid for Orchard with Cypresses at Christie's in 2022.

notes.The Starry Night: It has been at the Museum of Modern Art in New York since 1941, so it was not for sale.
notes.Irises: Irises set a world record of $53.9m at Sotheby's in 1987 and is now at the Getty Museum in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Sotheby's settles Van Gogh claim before sale
items.summary: On 17 November, the day before its New York sale, Sotheby's said the sellers and the Fischer heirs had reached an agreement over Blossoming Chestnut Trees.
items.question: Heirs of which Berlin publisher reached a deal over a Van Gogh estimated at $180m?
items.explain: Samuel and Hedwig Fischer owned the painting from 1909, and their heirs say its 1936 sale happened under Nazi persecution; the terms of the deal were not disclosed.

items.headline: Alfred Wallis, the fisherman who inspired St Ives
items.summary: Pallant House Gallery in Chichester opened 'Alfred Wallis: An Artists' Artist' on 21 November, showing his influence on British modernists.
items.question: Before taking up painting in his seventies, Alfred Wallis worked as what?
items.explain: Self-taught, he painted boats on scraps of cardboard, and Ben Nicholson and Christopher Wood befriended him in St Ives in 1928.

items.headline: Van Eyck's portraits reunited in London
items.summary: 'Van Eyck: The Portraits' opened at the National Gallery in London on 21 November and runs until 11 April 2027.
items.question: Whose portraits are on show at the National Gallery in London until April?
items.explain: The first exhibition devoted to Jan van Eyck's portraits, including the gallery's own Arnolfini Portrait.

items.headline: Peggy Guggenheim's London years at the RA
items.summary: Since 21 November the Royal Academy in London has looked at her London gallery, Guggenheim Jeune (1938–39).
items.question: Peggy Guggenheim's London gallery gave the first UK solo show to which artist?
items.explain: Guggenheim Jeune, at 30 Cork Street, hosted Kandinsky's first UK solo exhibition.

items.headline: Cézanne's Arlequin sells for $111m
items.summary: Arlequin sold for $111m with fees at Sotheby's New York on 18 November, short of Cézanne's auction record of about $138m, set in 2022.
items.question: Who posed for Cézanne's Arlequin, sold for $111m in New York?
items.explain: Paul junior modelled for Cézanne's harlequin paintings of 1888 to 1890, which Sotheby's says were inspired by the Mardi Gras parades of his childhood in Aix-en-Provence.

notes.His wife, Hortense: Hortense Fiquet sat for many portraits by Cézanne, but not this one.
notes.The writer Émile Zola: Zola was Cézanne's school friend in Aix-en-Provence, but he did not pose for this painting.
notes.The painter Camille Pissarro: Pissarro was Cézanne's mentor, not the model.

items.headline: Hilma af Klint painting sets a Nordic auction record
items.summary: Her 1920 abstract painting Ser III No. 5 sold for 128.9m Swedish kronor (about $12.7m) at Bukowskis in Stockholm on 19 November.
items.question: Which Swedish artist’s 1920 abstract painting just sold for about $12.7m?
items.explain: Hilma af Klint painted it in January 1920, and it made more than 16 times its top estimate; Bukowskis says no artwork has sold for more at auction in the Nordic countries.

notes.Carl Larsson: Larsson is loved for his cosy watercolours of Swedish family life, not abstract paintings.
notes.Anders Zorn: Zorn was a Swedish portrait painter famous for his bathers and society portraits.

items.headline: Venice Biennale closes after a record turnout of nations
items.summary: The 61st Venice Biennale, In Minor Keys, closed on 22 November after drawing 714,015 visitors.
items.question: What record did the 2026 Venice Biennale set?
items.explain: A record 100 countries had their own national exhibitions at this edition.

notes.Longest run ever: It actually ran about three weeks shorter than earlier editions, from 9 May to 22 November.
notes.First edition held outside Venice: This edition was held in Venice, the city that gives the Biennale its name.
